AlternateTargets: the person above and beyond Buddha
one who has gone beyond Buddha
Senses.Note: Four deployments span four independent works and distinguish this formula from general beyond-language.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師謂眾曰。知有佛向上人方有語話分。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T51/T51n2076.xml). Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp. Dongshan Liangjie tells the assembly that knowing the person beyond Buddha gives a share in speech, then answers the monk’s exact question “not ordinary.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 萬松道：體得佛向上人，方無說話分。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1307.xml). Elder Wansong’s Commentary and Chanted Remarks on Master Tiantong Jue’s Picking Up Ancient Cases: Record of Requests for Instruction. Wansong Xingxiu directly says that realizing the person beyond Buddha leaves no share in speech.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。舉：「洞山曰：『體得佛向上事，方有些子語話分。』僧問：『如何是佛向上人？』山曰：『非佛。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB369.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhe’an Fan. An unnamed monk in the Dongshan case asks the exact question; Zhe’an Jingfan raises the case and Dongshan Liangjie answers “not Buddha.” Unlinked context figure: Zhe’an Jingfan (later-raiser); identity and role are preserved here without a broken ContextMasters link.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: An unnamed monk in the quoted Dongshan case utters the exact headword-bearing question; Zhe’an Jingfan raises the case and Dongshan Liangjie responds.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是佛向上人？師曰：不帶容。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X81/X81n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 1–33). An unnamed monk asks Longjun directly who the person beyond Buddha is; Longjun answers “not admitting appearance.”

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The exact headword occurs in 問, making the unnamed monk its utterer; the enclosing heading identifies Longjun as respondent, not utterer of the headword.

Senses.Explanation: The person beyond Buddha is the person whom the records place on the far side even of the designation “Buddha.” Dongshan makes this a condition for having any share in speech and answers that such a person is “not Buddha”; later masters raise and test that formula rather than turning it into a higher religious rank. Dongshan states the formula and answers an anonymous questioner; Wansong reopens the case and asks whether such a person even understands question and answer; Zhe’an raises Dongshan and Yunmen before refusing to establish either above or below; and an unnamed monk asks Longjun directly for this person.
